claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has significant inherent porosity.
Porosity limits the mechanical or structural integrity of conventionally prepared ZrB2 under service conditions.
Porosity-related structural weaknesses cause eventual failure in liquid plating environments.
Adding a reactive liquid-phase precursor or sintering aid to ZrB2 powder will permit densification well below 2300 °C.
The precursor reacts during sintering to form a transient liquid phase.
The transient liquid phase enhances rearrangement of ZrB2 particles.
The transient liquid phase promotes neck formation and faster, more uniform interparticle bonding.
Enhanced particle rearrangement and bonding produce a denser ZrB2 microstructure with fewer defects and less microscale porosity.
Reduced porosity improves the strength and integrity of ZrB2 during exposure to an aggressive liquid plating bath.
Liquid plating baths exploit microstructural flaws in ZrB2.
Reducing porosity will reduce hole formation during prolonged liquid-plating exposure.
The intervention may lower the sintering temperature by several hundred degrees relative to 2300 °C.
Aid-modified ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
Aid-modified ZrB2 will experience fewer holes and less failure during prolonged liquid-plating exposure than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The effectiveness of the intervention may depend on the precursor's compatibility, concentration, and reactivity with ZrB2.
